# Project Architecture

> **Living document.** Aktualizowany na żywo w trakcie warsztatu, nie jest dokumentem końcowym.

# Kontekst biznesowy

Retail Operations Portal — system back-office do obsługi produktów, zamówień, oraz procesu promocji handlowej

# Drivery architektoniczne

| ID  | Driver                                                                              | Kategoria          | Źródło        |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------- |
| D1  | Czas wdrożenia zmiany w regułach promocji musi spaść z ~3 tyg. do < 3 dni           | Time-to-market     | Product Owner |
| D2  | Zespoły Pricing i Catalog nie mogą wzajemnie blokować się przy wydaniu              | Autonomia zespołów | Tech Lead     |
| D3  | Częściowa awaria (np. serwis rekomendacji) nie może blokować całego ekranu promocji | Resilience         | Operacje      |
| D4  | Nowi dostawcy frontendu (zespół B2B) muszą móc dołączyć bez przepisywania shella    | Rozszerzalność     | Architekt     |

# Ownership map

| Krok procesu           | Domena                     | Zespół        | Pakiet |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------- | ------ |
| Wybór produktów        | Catalog                    | Catalog Team  | _TBD_  |
| Reguły i ceny          | Pricing & Promotions       | Pricing Team  | _TBD_  |
| Walidacja → akceptacja | Pricing & Promotions       | Pricing Team  | _TBD_  |
| Aktywacja/publikacja   | Pricing & Promotions       | Pricing Team  | _TBD_  |
| Raportowanie           | Platform / Shared Services | Platform Team | _TBD_  |

> Pełny podział na bounded context (14) i domeny (4) z uzasadnieniem: [docs/context-map/context-map.md](./context-map/context-map.md).

```
In the workspace c:\Projects\bottega-frontend-architecture-rossmann, explore the folder retail-operations-portal/src thoroughly. I need a detailed inventory to plan a migration from a flat structure (api/, store/, pages/, types.ts) into 4 domain modules (product-catalog, product-pricing, sales-fulfilment, platform/shared) per an ADR.

Report back with:
1. Full list of files in src/api/, src/store/, src/pages/ (and subfolders), src/components/, src/layout/, src/lib/, src/mock-data/, plus src/types.ts, src/routes.tsx, src/App.tsx, src/main.tsx — as a directory tree with file names (no need to dump full contents of every file).
2. Contents of src/types.ts in full (or if very large, a summary of every exported type/interface with which bounded context it maps to, based on: Catalog(Product,Category), Pricing(PricingRule), Promotions(Promotion + validation/approval fields), Customer Segments(CustomerSegment), Orders & Returns(Order, ReturnRequest), Warehouse & Suppliers(WarehouseStock, Supplier), Reports, Notifications(Notification), Audit Log(AuditLogEntry), Identity/Users(User, UserRole), Feature Flags(FeatureFlag)).
3. For each file under src/store/ (likely Redux slices) — what domain/entity it manages and what it imports/exports.
4. For each file under src/api/ — what domain/entity it manages (e.g. products.ts, promotions.ts, pricingRules.ts, customerSegments.ts, orders.ts, returns.ts, warehouse.ts, suppliers.ts, notifications.ts, auditLog.ts, users.ts, featureFlags.ts) and any cross-domain imports (e.g. does promotions.ts import from products.ts or pricingRules.ts?).
5. Contents of src/routes.tsx in full — to understand route-to-page mapping.
6. Whether there's an existing ESLint config (eslint.config.* or .eslintrc*) at the retail-operations-portal root, and its current rules (especially anything about import restrictions/boundaries, e.g. eslint-plugin-boundaries or import/no-restricted-paths).
7. Check retail-operations-portal/tsconfig.app.json or tsconfig.json for path aliases (e.g. "@/*") currently configured.
8. List src/pages/ subfolders/files and map each page to a likely bounded context.
9. Check src/store/ for the root store setup file (e.g. store/index.ts) to see how slices are combined/registered.
10. Note any cross-domain imports you find in components/ or lib/ that would need to move to a shared/platform module vs staying domain-specific.

Be thorough and precise — quote actual file paths and actual import statements you find, don't guess. This is read-only research, do not modify any files.
```

# eslint/no-restricted-importsRestriction


### What it doesPermalink to “What it does”


This rule allows you to specify imports that you don’t want to use in your
application. It applies to static imports and to dynamic `import()` with a string-literal source; computed sources like `import(bar)` are ignored.


### Why is this bad?Permalink to “Why is this bad?”


Some imports might not make sense in a particular environment. For example,
Node.js’ fs module would not make sense in an environment that didn’t have a file
system.


Some modules provide similar or identical functionality, think lodash and
underscore. Your project may have standardized on a module. You want to make sure that
the other alternatives are not being used as this would unnecessarily bloat the
project and provide a higher maintenance cost of two dependencies when one
would suffice.


...
...
# eslint/no-restricted-importsRestriction
...
### ExamplesPermalink to “Examples”


Examples of incorrect code for this rule:

 js 
```
/* no-restricted-imports: ["error", "disallowed-import"] */

import foo from "disallowed-import";
export * from "disallowed-import";
```

Examples of correct code for this rule:

 js 
```
/* no-restricted-imports: ["error", "fs"] */

import crypto from "crypto";
export * from "bar";
```

...
...
# eslint/no-restricted-importsRestriction
...

# Plan: Migrate retail-operations-portal to 4 domain modules (ADR 0000)

Implements ADR [0000-podzial-na-moduly-domenowe.md](docs/adr/0000-podzial-na-moduly-domenowe.md): split the flat
`retail-operations-portal/src` (api/, store/, pages/, types.ts) into 4 physical modules
(`product-catalog`, `product-pricing`, `sales-fulfilment`, `platform`) + a `shared/` generic kit +
an `app/` composition root, with oxlint-enforced import boundaries.

## Confirmed decisions (from user)
- Split `platform/shared` ADR name into two real folders: `modules/platform` (business-generic
  contexts: Reports, Notifications, Audit Log, Identity/Users, Feature Flags) + `shared/` (pure
  technical UI kit/hooks/utils, importable by everyone, imports nothing from `modules/`).
- Composition root (App.tsx, main.tsx, routes.tsx, root store.ts, DashboardPage.tsx) lives at
  top-level `src/app/`, outside all modules.
- Migrate all 4 modules in one pass (not phased by driver priority).
- Boundary enforcement: **keep oxlint** (repo already uses only oxlint, no ESLint config exists).
  Verified oxlint does NOT support `eslint-plugin-boundaries` (not in its built-in plugin list;
  JS-plugin ESLint-compat mode is alpha/unverified for this plugin) — so do NOT add ESLint.
  Instead use oxlint's built-in `eslint/no-restricted-imports` rule (patterns/regex + paths) plus
  oxlint's **nested config** feature (`.oxlintrc.json` per folder, not auto-merged) to get
  directional, per-module boundaries.

## Current state (verified via Explore)
- No cross-imports today between `api/*.ts` files or between `store/*Slice.ts` files — each only
  imports its own type from flat `src/types.ts` + shared `delay.ts`/hooks.
- Only 2 real cross-domain code dependencies exist today (verified, not guessed):
  1. `PromotionWizardPage`/`PricingRuleForm` (Promotions/Pricing) use `ProductPicker`, `Product`,
     `Category`, `listProducts`, `listCategories` (Catalog) — matches context-map's flagged
     "Catalog → Promotions/Pricing, raw ID, no ACL" hotspot.
  2. `PromotionDetailsPage` (Promotions) imports `auditLog.ts` + `AuditTrailList` (platform).
- No other cross-module code dependency exists today (e.g. sales-fulfilment never imports Catalog
  despite `WarehouseStock.productId` conceptually referencing it — left as an open ADR question,
  do not invent an import for it).
- Path alias `@/*` → `./src/*` already configured in tsconfig.app.json/tsconfig.json + vite.config.ts.
- `src/routes.tsx` is the single router config importing all 20 pages.
- `src/store/store.ts` is the single root reducer registering all 15 slices.

## Target folder structure
```
src/
  app/                       # composition root, not a module: App.tsx, main.tsx, routes.tsx,
                              # store.ts (root reducer), DashboardPage.tsx
  modules/
    product-catalog/         # Catalog, Import/Export
      api/ store/ pages/ components/ mock-data/ types.ts index.ts
    product-pricing/         # Pricing, Promotions, Customer Segments, Validation Queue, Approvals
      api/ store/ pages/ components/ mock-data/ types.ts index.ts
    sales-fulfilment/         # Orders & Returns, Warehouse & Suppliers
      api/ store/ pages/ mock-data/ types.ts index.ts
    platform/                 # Reports, Notifications, Audit Log, Identity/Users, Feature Flags
      api/ store/ pages/ components/ mock-data/ types.ts index.ts
  shared/                     # generic technical kit, no business meaning
    components/ (DataTable, SimpleListPage, ConfirmationModal, AppErrorBoundary, KpiCard,
                 StatusBadge, GlobalSearch, ui/*)
    store/ (createListSlice.ts, hooks.ts, useLoadList.ts)
    lib/ (utils.ts, delay.ts)
    types.ts (ID)
  layout/                     # unchanged, stays top-level (uses platform's NotificationBell/UserMenu)
```
Each module's `index.ts` is its ONLY public API surface: re-exports types, api functions needed by
other allowed consumers, slice reducers (for `app/store.ts` to compose), and pages (for
`app/routes.tsx`). No other file may be deep-imported from outside the module.

## Allowed cross-module dependency directions (derived strictly from current code, not guessed)
- `product-catalog` → depends on nothing else.
- `product-pricing` → may depend on `product-catalog` (ProductPicker/Product/Category) and
  `platform` (auditLog/AuditTrailList). Must not depend on `sales-fulfilment`.
- `sales-fulfilment` → depends on nothing else.
- `platform` → depends on nothing else (generic, confirmed by context-map: no integrations today).
- `shared` → depends on nothing under `modules/`.
- `app/` (composition root, outside `modules/`) → may import any module's public `index.ts`.

## oxlint boundary config design
Root `retail-operations-portal/.oxlintrc.json` (new file — repo has none today):
- `eslint/no-restricted-imports` with:
  - `patterns: [{ regex: "^@/modules/[^/]+/.+" }]` — blocks any deep import into another module's
    internals; only the bare `@/modules/<name>` (→ index.ts) is allowed.
  - `patterns: [{ regex: "^(\\.\\./)+modules/" }]` — blocks relative-path traversal that escapes
    into `modules/`, forcing the `@/modules/<name>` alias for all cross-module imports.

Nested `.oxlintrc.json` per module (extends root, adds directional `paths` restriction — see
directions above):
- `src/modules/product-catalog/.oxlintrc.json` → restrict paths: product-pricing, sales-fulfilment, platform
- `src/modules/product-pricing/.oxlintrc.json` → restrict paths: sales-fulfilment
- `src/modules/sales-fulfilment/.oxlintrc.json` → restrict paths: product-catalog, product-pricing, platform
- `src/modules/platform/.oxlintrc.json` → restrict paths: product-catalog, product-pricing, sales-fulfilment
- `src/shared/.oxlintrc.json` → restrict pattern blocking any `@/modules/` import at all
- `src/app/` gets no nested config (inherits root only) — it's the only place allowed to import
  every module's public API.

## Steps

**Phase 1 — Scaffolding & shared/ extraction (foundational, must land first)**
1. Create empty module folder skeletons (`modules/{product-catalog,product-pricing,sales-fulfilment,platform}/{api,store,pages,components?,mock-data,types.ts,index.ts}`) and `shared/{components,store,lib,types.ts}`, `app/`.
2. Move `lib/utils.ts`, `api/delay.ts` → `shared/lib/`; `store/createListSlice.ts`, `store/hooks.ts`, `store/useLoadList.ts` → `shared/store/`; generic components (`DataTable`, `SimpleListPage`, `ConfirmationModal`, `AppErrorBoundary`, `KpiCard`, `StatusBadge`, `GlobalSearch`, `components/ui/*`) → `shared/components/`. Update all importers (many pages/components use these) to `@/shared/...`.
3. Extract `ID` type into `shared/types.ts`.
4. Add root `.oxlintrc.json` with the deep-import + relative-traversal restriction rules above.

**Phase 2 — product-catalog module** (*depends on Phase 1*)
5. Move `api/products.ts`, `api/categories.ts` + `mock-data/products.json`, `mock-data/categories.json` → `modules/product-catalog/api|mock-data/`.
6. Move `store/productsSlice.ts`, `store/categoriesSlice.ts` → `modules/product-catalog/store/`.
7. Move pages `ProductsPage`, `ProductDetailsPage`, `CategoriesPage`, `ImportExportPage` and component `FileImportWidget` → `modules/product-catalog/pages|components/`.
8. Move `ProductPicker.tsx` → `modules/product-catalog/components/` (consumed externally by product-pricing).
9. Extract `Product`, `Category` into `modules/product-catalog/types.ts`; remove from flat `src/types.ts`.
10. Write `modules/product-catalog/index.ts` public API: types, `listProducts`/`listCategories`/etc., slice reducers+actions, `ProductPicker`, pages.
11. Add nested `.oxlintrc.json` (restrict paths: product-pricing, sales-fulfilment, platform).

**Phase 3 — product-pricing module** (*depends on Phase 2 for Catalog's public API; parallel with Phase 4/5*)

import { useEffect } from "react";
import type { ActionCreatorWithPayload } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { useAppDispatch } from "./hooks";

// Fetches once (if not already loaded) and stores the result via the slice's setItems action.
export function useLoadList<T>(
  loaded: boolean,
  fetchFn: () => Promise<T[]>,
  setItems: ActionCreatorWithPayload<T[]>,
) {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  useEffect(() => {
    if (loaded) return;
    fetchFn().then((items) => dispatch(setItems(items)));
  }, [loaded, fetchFn, setItems, dispatch]);
}
```
</details></tool-use>

# bottega-frontend-architecture-rossmann repo structure

- Single git repo at workspace root; `retail-operations-portal/` is a nested subfolder with its
  own `package.json`/`node_modules` (not a separate repo). Terminal cwd can persist as either the
  workspace root or `retail-operations-portal/` across tool calls in the same session — always
  `pwd` first if unsure before `cd`-prefixing a command, since a redundant `cd retail-operations-portal`
  when already there fails silently (newline-separated bash commands don't stop on error) and
  leaves later relative paths resolving from the wrong place.
- Docs are canonical source of truth: read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` before any architecture work.
  `docs/adr/`, `docs/context-map/context-map.md` also authoritative. Ignore `./exercises`,
  `./docs/architecture-reports` (not part of the project).
- Only linter in `retail-operations-portal` is **oxlint** (no ESLint). It supports nested
  `.oxlintrc.json` per directory (nearest wins, NOT auto-merged — child must `extends` parent and
  restate same-key rules) and the `no-restricted-imports` rule (patterns=regex, paths=exact) which
  is sufficient to enforce module import boundaries without `eslint-plugin-boundaries` (oxlint
  doesn't support it).
- Path alias `@/*` → `retail-operations-portal/src/*` (tsconfig + vite.config.ts).
- When `git mv`-ing a file, check for BOTH alias imports (`@/...`) AND relative imports (`./x`,
  `../x`) — both from the moved file and pointing to it from files left behind. Grep for both
  styles after every move before trusting a build.

```

import productsRaw from "@/mock-data/products.json";
import type { Product } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, Product>(productsRaw.map((p) => [p.id, p as Product]));

export async function listProducts(): Promise<Product[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getProduct(id: string): Promise<Product | null> {
  await delay();
  return db.get(id) ?? null;
}

export async function updateProduct(id: string, patch: Partial<Product>): Promise<Product> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Product ${id} not found`);
  const next = { ...current, ...patch };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

// Stub: real implementation would parse the file and upsert rows into `db`.
export async function importProductsFromCsv(_file: File): Promise<{ imported: number }> {
  await delay(600);
  return { imported: 0 };
}

export async function exportProducts(): Promise<Product[]> {
  await delay(400);
  return [...db.values()];
}
```

import { useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/shared/components/ui/button";
import { Input } from "@/shared/components/ui/input";
import { Progress } from "@/shared/components/ui/progress";

interface FileImportWidgetProps {
  onImport: (file: File) => Promise<{ imported: number }>;
  onExport?: () => void;
}

// Small and self-contained — another good candidate for a Web Component comparison (Dzień 2 A3).
export function FileImportWidget({ onImport, onExport }: FileImportWidgetProps) {
  const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = useState<string | null>(null);

  async function handleImport() {
    if (!file) return;
    setBusy(true);
    setResult(null);
    try {
      const { imported } = await onImport(file);
      setResult(`Zaimportowano ${imported} rekordów.`);
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <Input
          type="file"
          accept=".csv"
          onChange={(e) => setFile(e.target.files?.[0] ?? null)}
          className="max-w-xs"
        />
        <Button onClick={handleImport} disabled={!file || busy}>
          Importuj
        </Button>
        {onExport && (
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={onExport}>
            Eksportuj
          </Button>
        )}
      </div>
      {busy && <Progress value={null} className="w-64" />}
      {result && <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{result}</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import { SimpleListPage } from "@/shared/components/SimpleListPage";
import { listWarehouseStock } from "@/api/warehouse";
import { listProducts } from "@/api/products";
import { setWarehouseStock } from "@/store/warehouseSlice";
import { setProducts } from "@/store/productsSlice";
import { useAppSelector } from "@/shared/store/hooks";
import { useLoadList } from "@/shared/store/useLoadList";

// Referenced from ProductDetailsPage — same data shown two ways (cross-domain coupling material).
export function WarehousePage() {
  const stock = useAppSelector((s) => s.warehouse.items);
  useLoadList(useAppSelector((s) => s.warehouse.loaded), listWarehouseStock, setWarehouseStock);
  const products = useAppSelector((s) => s.products.items);
  useLoadList(useAppSelector((s) => s.products.loaded), listProducts, setProducts);

  const productName = (id: string) => products.find((p) => p.id === id)?.name ?? id;

  return (
    <SimpleListPage
      title="Stany magazynowe"
      columns={[
        { key: "product", header: "Produkt", render: (w) => productName(w.productId) },
        { key: "location", header: "Lokalizacja", render: (w) => w.location },
        { key: "quantity", header: "Ilość", render: (w) => w.quantity },
        { key: "reserved", header: "Zarezerwowane", render: (w) => w.reserved },
        { key: "available", header: "Dostępne", render: (w) => w.quantity - w.reserved },
      ]}
      rows={stock}
      getRowId={(w) => w.id}
      searchText={(w) => productName(w.productId)}
    />
  );
}
```

import pricingRulesRaw from "@/mock-data/pricingRules.json";
import type { PricingRule } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, PricingRule>(pricingRulesRaw.map((r) => [r.id, r as PricingRule]));

export async function listPricingRules(): Promise<PricingRule[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getPricingRule(id: string): Promise<PricingRule | null> {
  await delay();
  return db.get(id) ?? null;
}

export async function addPricingRule(rule: Omit<PricingRule, "id">): Promise<PricingRule> {
  await delay();
  const id = `pr-${db.size + 1}-${Date.now()}`;
  const next: PricingRule = { ...rule, id };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function removePricingRule(id: string): Promise<void> {
  await delay();
  db.delete(id);
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import promotionsRaw from "@/mock-data/promotions.json";
import type { Promotion } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, Promotion>(promotionsRaw.map((p) => [p.id, p as Promotion]));

export async function listPromotions(): Promise<Promotion[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getPromotion(id: string): Promise<Promotion | null> {
  await delay();
  return db.get(id) ?? null;
}

export async function createPromotion(
  draft: Omit<Promotion, "id" | "status">,
): Promise<Promotion> {
  await delay();
  const id = `promo-${db.size + 1}-${Date.now()}`;
  const next: Promotion = { ...draft, id, status: "draft" };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function updatePromotion(id: string, patch: Partial<Promotion>): Promise<Promotion> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Promotion ${id} not found`);
  const next = { ...current, ...patch };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function selectProductsForPromotion(
  id: string,
  productIds: string[],
): Promise<Promotion> {
  return updatePromotion(id, { productIds });
}

export async function submitPromotionForValidation(id: string): Promise<Promotion> {
  return updatePromotion(id, { status: "pending_validation" });
}

import type { Promotion, PromotionStatus } from "@/types";
import { cn } from "@/shared/lib/utils";

const STEPS: { status: PromotionStatus; label: string }[] = [
  { status: "draft", label: "Szkic" },
  { status: "pending_validation", label: "Walidacja" },
  { status: "pending_approval", label: "Akceptacja" },
  { status: "active", label: "Aktywacja" },
];

// Visualizes where a promotion is in the wybór→reguły→walidacja→akceptacja→aktywacja process.
export function PromotionStatusTimeline({ promotion }: { promotion: Promotion }) {
  const archived = promotion.status === "archived";
  const currentIndex = archived
    ? STEPS.length - 1
    : STEPS.findIndex((s) => s.status === promotion.status);

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      {STEPS.map((step, idx) => (
        <div key={step.status} className="flex flex-1 items-center gap-2">
          <div
            className={cn(
              "flex h-7 w-7 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border text-xs font-medium",
              idx <= currentIndex
                ? "border-primary bg-primary text-primary-foreground"
                : "border-border bg-background text-muted-foreground",
            )}
          >
            {idx + 1}
```

import { Button } from "@/shared/components/ui/button";
import { useAppSelector } from "@/shared/store/hooks";

interface ApprovalActionBarProps {
  onApprove: () => void;
  onReject: () => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
}

// Role-gated: only admin/manager can approve or reject (Dzień 3 auth/permissions material).
export function ApprovalActionBar({ onApprove, onReject, disabled }: ApprovalActionBarProps) {
  const role = useAppSelector((s) => s.currentUser.role);
  const canDecide = role === "admin" || role === "manager";

  if (!canDecide) {
    return <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Twoja rola nie pozwala na akceptację.</p>;
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <Button onClick={onApprove} disabled={disabled}>
        Zaakceptuj
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={onReject} disabled={disabled}>
        Odrzuć
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}

import ordersRaw from "@/mock-data/orders.json";
import type { Order } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, Order>(ordersRaw.map((o) => [o.id, o as Order]));

export async function listOrders(): Promise<Order[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function approveOrder(id: string): Promise<Order> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Order ${id} not found`);
  const next: Order = { ...current, status: "approved" };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function cancelOrder(id: string, _reason: string): Promise<Order> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Order ${id} not found`);
  const next: Order = { ...current, status: "cancelled" };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import warehouseRaw from "@/mock-data/warehouse.json";
import type { WarehouseStock } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, WarehouseStock>(warehouseRaw.map((w) => [w.id, w as WarehouseStock]));

export async function listWarehouseStock(): Promise<WarehouseStock[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getStockForProduct(productId: string): Promise<WarehouseStock[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()].filter((w) => w.productId === productId);
}

export async function adjustStock(id: string, delta: number): Promise<WarehouseStock> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Warehouse record ${id} not found`);
  const next = { ...current, quantity: current.quantity + delta };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}
```

import suppliersRaw from "@/mock-data/suppliers.json";
import type { Supplier } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, Supplier>(suppliersRaw.map((s) => [s.id, s as Supplier]));

export async function listSuppliers(): Promise<Supplier[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getSupplier(id: string): Promise<Supplier | null> {
  await delay();
  return db.get(id) ?? null;
}

export async function updateSupplier(id: string, patch: Partial<Supplier>): Promise<Supplier> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Supplier ${id} not found`);
  const next = { ...current, ...patch };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

import pricingRulesRaw from "@/mock-data/pricingRules.json";
import type { PricingRule } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, PricingRule>(pricingRulesRaw.map((r) => [r.id, r as PricingRule]));

export async function listPricingRules(): Promise<PricingRule[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getPricingRule(id: string): Promise<PricingRule | null> {
  await delay();
  return db.get(id) ?? null;
}

export async function addPricingRule(rule: Omit<PricingRule, "id">): Promise<PricingRule> {
  await delay();
  const id = `pr-${db.size + 1}-${Date.now()}`;
  const next: PricingRule = { ...rule, id };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function removePricingRule(id: string): Promise<void> {
  await delay();
  db.delete(id);
}
```

import promotionsRaw from "@/mock-data/promotions.json";
import type { Promotion } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, Promotion>(promotionsRaw.map((p) => [p.id, p as Promotion]));

export async function listPromotions(): Promise<Promotion[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function getPromotion(id: string): Promise<Promotion | null> {
  await delay();
  return db.get(id) ?? null;
}

export async function createPromotion(
  draft: Omit<Promotion, "id" | "status">,
): Promise<Promotion> {
  await delay();
  const id = `promo-${db.size + 1}-${Date.now()}`;
  const next: Promotion = { ...draft, id, status: "draft" };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function updatePromotion(id: string, patch: Partial<Promotion>): Promise<Promotion> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(id);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Promotion ${id} not found`);
  const next = { ...current, ...patch };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}

export async function selectProductsForPromotion(
  id: string,
  productIds: string[],
): Promise<Promotion> {
  return updatePromotion(id, { productIds });
}

export async function submitPromotionForValidation(id: string): Promise<Promotion> {
  return updatePromotion(id, { status: "pending_validation" });
}

import type { Promotion, PromotionStatus } from "@/types";
import { cn } from "@/shared/lib/utils";

const STEPS: { status: PromotionStatus; label: string }[] = [
  { status: "draft", label: "Szkic" },
  { status: "pending_validation", label: "Walidacja" },
  { status: "pending_approval", label: "Akceptacja" },
  { status: "active", label: "Aktywacja" },
];

// Visualizes where a promotion is in the wybór→reguły→walidacja→akceptacja→aktywacja process.
export function PromotionStatusTimeline({ promotion }: { promotion: Promotion }) {
  const archived = promotion.status === "archived";
  const currentIndex = archived
    ? STEPS.length - 1
    : STEPS.findIndex((s) => s.status === promotion.status);

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      {STEPS.map((step, idx) => (
        <div key={step.status} className="flex flex-1 items-center gap-2">
          <div
            className={cn(
              "flex h-7 w-7 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border text-xs font-medium",
              idx <= currentIndex
                ? "border-primary bg-primary text-primary-foreground"
                : "border-border bg-background text-muted-foreground",
            )}
          >
            {idx + 1}
          </div>
          <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{step.label}</span>
          {idx < STEPS.length - 1 && <div className="h-px flex-1 bg-border" />}
        </div>
      ))}
      {archived && <span className="ml-2 text-xs text-muted-foreground">(zarchiwizowana)</span>}
    </div>
  );
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import type { ValidationResult } from "@/types";
import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "@/shared/components/ui/alert";
import { Button } from "@/shared/components/ui/button";

interface ValidationResultsPanelProps {
  validation?: ValidationResult;
  onRunValidation: () => void;
  running?: boolean;
}

export function ValidationResultsPanel({
  validation,
  onRunValidation,
  running,
}: ValidationResultsPanelProps) {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <Button onClick={onRunValidation} disabled={running}>
        {running ? "Walidacja w toku..." : "Uruchom walidację"}
      </Button>
      {validation && (
        <Alert variant={validation.passed ? "default" : "destructive"}>
          <AlertTitle>
            {validation.passed ? "Walidacja zakończona pomyślnie" : "Walidacja wykryła problemy"}
          </AlertTitle>
          <AlertDescription>
            {validation.issues.length > 0 ? (
              <ul className="list-disc pl-4">
                {validation.issues.map((issue) => (
                  <li key={issue}>{issue}</li>
                ))}
              </ul>
            ) : (
              "Brak zastrzeżeń."
            )}
            <div className="mt-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
              Sprawdzono: {new Date(validation.checkedAt).toLocaleString("pl-PL")}
            </div>
          </AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

import { Button } from "@/shared/components/ui/button";
import { useAppSelector } from "@/shared/store/hooks";

interface ApprovalActionBarProps {
  onApprove: () => void;
  onReject: () => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
}

// Role-gated: only admin/manager can approve or reject (Dzień 3 auth/permissions material).
export function ApprovalActionBar({ onApprove, onReject, disabled }: ApprovalActionBarProps) {
  const role = useAppSelector((s) => s.currentUser.role);
  const canDecide = role === "admin" || role === "manager";

  if (!canDecide) {
    return <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Twoja rola nie pozwala na akceptację.</p>;
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <Button onClick={onApprove} disabled={disabled}>
        Zaakceptuj
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={onReject} disabled={disabled}>
        Odrzuć
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}

import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { auditLogSlice } from "./auditLogSlice";
import { currentUserSlice } from "./currentUserSlice";
import { customerSegmentsSlice } from "./customerSegmentsSlice";
import { featureFlagsSlice } from "./featureFlagsSlice";
import { notificationsSlice } from "./notificationsSlice";
import { pricingRulesSlice } from "./pricingRulesSlice";
import { productsSlice, categoriesSlice } from "@/modules/product-catalog";
import { promotionsSlice } from "./promotionsSlice";
import { ordersSlice, returnsSlice, suppliersSlice, warehouseSlice } from "@/modules/sales-fulfilment";
import { usersSlice } from "./usersSlice";

// One store for every domain — intentional "global store as the app's database" anti-pattern.
export const store = configureStore({
  reducer: {
    products: productsSlice.reducer,
    categories: categoriesSlice.reducer,
    suppliers: suppliersSlice.reducer,
    orders: ordersSlice.reducer,
    warehouse: warehouseSlice.reducer,
    pricingRules: pricingRulesSlice.reducer,
    promotions: promotionsSlice.reducer,
    customerSegments: customerSegmentsSlice.reducer,
    returns: returnsSlice.reducer,
    notifications: notificationsSlice.reducer,
    auditLog: auditLogSlice.reducer,
    users: usersSlice.reducer,
    featureFlags: featureFlagsSlice.reducer,
    currentUser: currentUserSlice.reducer,
  },
});

export type RootState = ReturnType<typeof store.getState>;
export type AppDispatch = typeof store.dispatch;
```

import { SimpleListPage } from "@/shared/components/SimpleListPage";
import { listWarehouseStock } from "@/api/warehouse";
import { listProducts, setProducts } from "@/modules/product-catalog";
import { setWarehouseStock } from "@/store/warehouseSlice";
import { useAppSelector } from "@/shared/store/hooks";
import { useLoadList } from "@/shared/store/useLoadList";

// Referenced from ProductDetailsPage — same data shown two ways (cross-domain coupling material).
export function WarehousePage() {
  const stock = useAppSelector((s) => s.warehouse.items);
  useLoadList(useAppSelector((s) => s.warehouse.loaded), listWarehouseStock, setWarehouseStock);
  const products = useAppSelector((s) => s.products.items);
  useLoadList(useAppSelector((s) => s.products.loaded), listProducts, setProducts);

  const productName = (id: string) => products.find((p) => p.id === id)?.name ?? id;

  return (
    <SimpleListPage
      title="Stany magazynowe"
      columns={[
        { key: "product", header: "Produkt", render: (w) => productName(w.productId) },
        { key: "location", header: "Lokalizacja", render: (w) => w.location },
        { key: "quantity", header: "Ilość", render: (w) => w.quantity },
        { key: "reserved", header: "Zarezerwowane", render: (w) => w.reserved },
        { key: "available", header: "Dostępne", render: (w) => w.quantity - w.reserved },
      ]}
      rows={stock}
      getRowId={(w) => w.id}
      searchText={(w) => productName(w.productId)}
    />
  );
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import auditLogRaw from "@/mock-data/auditLog.json";
import type { AuditLogEntry } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, AuditLogEntry>(auditLogRaw.map((a) => [a.id, a as AuditLogEntry]));

export async function listAuditLog(): Promise<AuditLogEntry[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()].sort((a, b) => b.timestamp.localeCompare(a.timestamp));
}

export async function addAuditLogEntry(entry: Omit<AuditLogEntry, "id">): Promise<AuditLogEntry> {
  await delay();
  const id = `audit-${db.size + 1}-${Date.now()}`;
  const next: AuditLogEntry = { ...entry, id };
  db.set(id, next);
  return next;
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import featureFlagsRaw from "@/mock-data/featureFlags.json";
import type { FeatureFlag } from "@/types";
import { delay } from "@/shared/lib/delay";

const db = new Map<string, FeatureFlag>(featureFlagsRaw.map((f) => [f.key, f]));

export async function listFeatureFlags(): Promise<FeatureFlag[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];
}

export async function toggleFeatureFlag(key: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<FeatureFlag> {
  await delay();
  const current = db.get(key);
  if (!current) throw new Error(`Feature flag ${key} not found`);
  const next = { ...current, enabled };
  db.set(key, next);
  return next;
}
```

export async function listNotifications(): Promise<Notification[]> {
  await delay();
  return [...db.values()];

export async function markNotificationRead(id: string): Promise<Notification> {

  const current = db.get(id);

import usersRaw from "@/mock-data/users.json";

export async function listUsers(): Promise<User[]> {

  admin: "Administrator",

export function UserMenu() {
  const user = useAppSelector((s) => s.currentUser);
  const initials = user.name
    .split(" ")
    .map((part) => part[0])
    .join("");

  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <Avatar className="size-8">
          <AvatarFallback>{initials}</AvatarFallback>
        </Avatar>
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>

        </DropdownMenuGroup>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />

import type { AuditLogEntry } from "@/types";

// Used by both PromotionDetailsPage (filtered to one entity) and the full /audit-log page.
export function AuditTrailList({ entries }: { entries: AuditLogEntry[] }) {
  if (entries.length === 0) {
    return <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Brak zdarzeń.</p>;
  }

  return (
    <ul className="space-y-2">
      {entries.map((entry) => (
        <li key={entry.id} className="border-b pb-2 text-sm last:border-0">
          <span className="font-medium">{entry.action}</span>{" "}
          <span className="text-muted-foreground">
            · {entry.entityType} {entry.entityId} · {entry.actor} ·{" "}
            {new Date(entry.timestamp).toLocaleString("pl-PL")}
          </span>
          {entry.details && <div className="text-muted-foreground">{entry.details}</div>}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { auditLogSlice } from "./auditLogSlice";
import { currentUserSlice } from "./currentUserSlice";
import { featureFlagsSlice } from "./featureFlagsSlice";
import { notificationsSlice } from "./notificationsSlice";
import { productsSlice, categoriesSlice } from "@/modules/product-catalog";
import { pricingRulesSlice, promotionsSlice, customerSegmentsSlice } from "@/modules/product-pricing";
import { ordersSlice, returnsSlice, suppliersSlice, warehouseSlice } from "@/modules/sales-fulfilment";
import { usersSlice } from "./usersSlice";

// One store for every domain — intentional "global store as the app's database" anti-pattern.
export const store = configureStore({
  reducer: {
    products: productsSlice.reducer,
    categories: categoriesSlice.reducer,
    suppliers: suppliersSlice.reducer,
    orders: ordersSlice.reducer,
    warehouse: warehouseSlice.reducer,
    pricingRules: pricingRulesSlice.reducer,
    promotions: promotionsSlice.reducer,
    customerSegments: customerSegmentsSlice.reducer,
    returns: returnsSlice.reducer,
    notifications: notificationsSlice.reducer,
    auditLog: auditLogSlice.reducer,
    users: usersSlice.reducer,
    featureFlags: featureFlagsSlice.reducer,
    currentUser: currentUserSlice.reducer,
  },
});

export type RootState = ReturnType<typeof store.getState>;
export type AppDispatch = typeof store.dispatch;
```

  const orders = useAppSelector((s) => s.orders.items);

  useLoadList(ordersLoaded, listOrders, setOrders);

import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { productsSlice, categoriesSlice } from "@/modules/product-catalog";
import { pricingRulesSlice, promotionsSlice, customerSegmentsSlice } from "@/modules/product-pricing";
import { ordersSlice, returnsSlice, suppliersSlice, warehouseSlice } from "@/modules/sales-fulfilment";
import {
  auditLogSlice,
  currentUserSlice,
  featureFlagsSlice,
  notificationsSlice,
  usersSlice,
} from "@/modules/platform";

// One store for every domain — intentional "global store as the app's database" anti-pattern.
export const store = configureStore({
  reducer: {
    products: productsSlice.reducer,
    categories: categoriesSlice.reducer,
    suppliers: suppliersSlice.reducer,
    orders: ordersSlice.reducer,
    warehouse: warehouseSlice.reducer,
    pricingRules: pricingRulesSlice.reducer,
    promotions: promotionsSlice.reducer,
    customerSegments: customerSegmentsSlice.reducer,
    returns: returnsSlice.reducer,
    notifications: notificationsSlice.reducer,
    auditLog: auditLogSlice.reducer,
    users: usersSlice.reducer,
    featureFlags: featureFlagsSlice.reducer,
    currentUser: currentUserSlice.reducer,
  },
});

export type RootState = ReturnType<typeof store.getState>;
export type AppDispatch = typeof store.dispatch;
```
</details></tool-use>

- Multi-line bash commands with many newline-separated (not `&&`-chained) commands can trigger a
  bracketed-paste terminal artifact (`bash: [200~: command not found`) that silently aborts the
  whole batch partway through, sometimes leaving stray duplicate/stale files behind. Always
  `&&`-chain batch `git mv` sequences on one logical line, and verify with `git status --short`
  / `ls` after every batch instead of assuming success from lack of error output.
- Stray stale/duplicate files at OLD paths have reappeared after `git mv` at least 3 times during
  the ADR-0000 module migration, including once with a single properly `&&`-chained command (no
  bracketed-paste error printed) — root cause not fully confirmed, suspect an editor/file-watcher
  on Windows re-materializing a recently-closed buffer. ALWAYS run `git status --short` after every
  `git mv` batch and look for unexpected `??` (untracked) entries reappearing at the old path, not
  just confirm the `R`/`RM` rename line — a clean rename line does not guarantee the old path is
  actually gone.
```
